subtasks.title: Uppercase-run walk + enriched onAdmittedTokens payload
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: the adjacency machinery exists — SpanEntry (src/pi/ingest.ts:109-122), WHITESPACE_GAP_RE = /^[ \t]+$/ (:128), splitRuns (:176-189), appendSegment (:206-247). The runs payload onAdmittedTokens: (runs: string[][]) => void (ingest.ts:258, IngestPipelineOptions :226-262) carries ONLY lowercase keys and is wired at src/pi/index.ts:211 → store.recordBigramRuns (store.ts:536). Shape-gate-rejected members never emit run entries, so they split runs naturally (layer-2 isSecretShaped). PITFALL (architecture/01 §9): layer-1 maskSecrets blanks secret windows to SPACES — a masked secret between two capitalized words must still break the run (conservative choice; pin in tests).
2. INPUT: CasingClass per occurrence from P1.M1.T1.S1; the existing SpanEntry/splitRuns stream in ingest.ts:416-497 (processText runs collection).
3. LOGIC: Implement spec 04 h2.26 run detection. A run = maximal sequence of ≥2 consecutive whole tokens on the same line, every token beginning with an uppercase ASCII letter, adjacent tokens separated by nothing but plain spaces/tabs (the SAME strict adjacency window as bigram capture — clause punctuation, quotes/brackets, digits/hexish, symbols, any intervening word, and newlines all break it). Runs are detected wherever they sit: line-initial and after-punctuation positions included — the structural-start exclusion does NOT apply to run detection. Each member must pass the shape gate; a secret-shaped/noise member splits the run around it. Widen the onAdmittedTokens payload to carry run membership + run casing (e.g. runs of {key, rawCasing} members — serializable, no spans needed); adapt the index.ts:211 wiring so recordBigramRuns keeps compiling (store consumes the enrichment in P1.M1.T2.S2 — until then pass-through/shim, tests stay green). Run-detection battery rides here: window breaks incl. 'ZorpWibbleEngine, quuxblat', secret split, masked-secret split, line-initial runs. Mocking: ingest tests use in-memory dictionary doubles per test/ingest.test.ts conventions.
4. OUTPUT: enriched run payload consumed by P1.M1.T3.S1 (admission override + chain-only set) and P1.M1.T2.S2 (series bigrams).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the new run-detection export (ingest.ts seam or src/core/segment.ts) and on the widened onAdmittedTokens payload contract. Rides with the work.

subtasks.title: Candidate casing tallies (additive migration, display kept temporarily)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Candidate lives at src/core/types.ts:19-33 (display = 'most recent casing seen'); store.upsert at src/core/store.ts:264-298 (create fills all 9 fields; merge bumps sessionCount/lastSeenOrdinal, existing.display = sighting.display at :291, sticky OR-ins for userTyped/properName, rankGroup = min). Nothing in score.ts reads display — salience/eviction unaffected (architecture/02-store-query-r1-r2.md §3). ~22 .display consumers stay green only if display survives until the resolver lands (inventory: 02 §5) — hence ADDITIVE here, subtractive in P1.M2.T1.S2.
2. INPUT: Sighting.casing from P1.M1.T1.S1 ('lower' | 'mid-cap' | 'structural-cap').

ADD to Candidate: capCount, lowerCount, capDisplay (most frequent capitalized form; ties → most recent sighting) — KEEP display populated as today so all consumers stay green. Upsert merge rules: a sentence-initial ('structural-cap') capitalized sighting contributes to capCount ONLY while the word has never been seen lowercase; the FIRST lowercase sighting removes those structural contributions PERMANENTLY (sticky seenLowercase flag in the merge; a capitalized sentence-initial form whose lowercase twin exists is dropped entirely — the lowercase form is the word; later structural caps never contribute again); 'mid-cap' sightings always count toward capCount and set/compete for capDisplay. Chain-only members never reach upsert (P1.M1.T3.S1 guards that — store must not see them). Store battery rides here: exact-object toEqual idiom (test/store.test.ts:86), twin-suppression permanence, capDisplay tie→recent. Mocking: none — pure store tests with hand-built Sighting literals.
4. OUTPUT: Candidate tally fields consumed by P1.M2.T1.S1 (resolver), P1.M2.T1.S2 (display removal), P1.M2.T3.S1 (/acwords), and P2.M1.T2.S2 (purity equality).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on Candidate's new casing fields in src/core/types.ts (semantics incl. the permanence rule; spec anchor 06 h2.43). Rides with the work.

subtasks.title: Series bigrams: BigramEntry/Successor extension + series-first top-3 retention
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: recordBigramRuns ALREADY EXISTS at src/core/store.ts:536-561 (takes runs: string[][] of lowercase keys; every adjacent pair counted in #bigrams; successor top-3 maintained by #bumpSuccessor :573-606 with successorBefore :140 — count desc, byte-lex asc; BIGRAM_CAP 10_000 with lazy eviction bigramSortKey = Math.log(count) + lastSeenOrdinal/50 (:136); eviction splices successors via #dropSuccessorFor :706-717). BigramEntry today = {count, lastSeenOrdinal} (:110); Successor = {next, count} (types.ts:54-60). Store adds NO window logic — runs arrive pre-chunked by ingest (architecture/02 §3, §8).
2. INPUT: enriched runs payload (run membership + run casing) from P1.M1.T1.S2; the chain-only member set from P1.M1.T3.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement spec 06 h3.6/h3.7 series extensions. Successor gains series?: boolean and nextDisplay?: string; BigramEntry gains the same. recordBigramRuns consumes the enriched payload: every adjacent pair inside a capitalized run is recorded as a series bigram — INCLUDING chain-only members (they were skipped at upsert but still form pairs) — each marked series and remembering the second word's run casing (nextDisplay). Retention: series entries rank above ordinary successors in the per-word top-3 (series first by count desc, then ordinary by count desc) so the 07 h2.53 'series first regardless of counts' offer rule is stable; same window-break rules and the same bigram cap/eviction as ordinary pairs. Battery rides here: series marking, chain-only inclusion, series-first retention, eviction parity (test/bigrams.test.ts:14-71 + test/successors.test.ts conventions). Mocking: none — pure store tests.
4. OUTPUT: Successor.series/nextDisplay + series-aware topSuccessors ordering, consumed by P1.M2.T2.S1/S2 (offers) and P1.M2.T3.S1 (/acwords), and covered by P2.M1.T2.S2 (purity).

subtasks.title: Run-member band bypass + conjugation-guard skip + top-band chain-only ceiling
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: admit() is pure f(draft, dictionary, opts) at src/core/score.ts:282-361; floor REJECT_COMMON_THRESHOLD = 30 (:109); rEff at :188-196. The admission memo (#computeAdmitMemo, ingest.ts:567-598) is token-intrinsic and MUST STAY CONTEXT-FREE — memoizing a run-member admission would permanently admit every later lowercase occurrence of that token (PRD's critical pitfall; architecture/01 §2). Structural fact: upserts are segment-scoped (#replayAdmitMemo :606-643) while runs finalize line/message-scoped (processText :416-497) — use the researcher-recommended low-risk path: keep eager upserts and apply run-derived admission effects at occurrence/run-finalization level (retro-override via store merge), NOT deferred upserts (architecture/00 §3.2). Conjugation-guard skip precedent: score.ts:317 (!draft.properName). PROPER_NOUN_ADMIT_CEILING = 30 (:152) branch at :303-310 is provably dead — leave retired-in-place, do NOT revive it.
2. INPUT: run membership from P1.M1.T1.S2's enriched payload.
3. LOGIC: Implement spec 04 h2.26/h2.28 run-member admission. Add baked constant PROPER_SERIES_TOP_BAND_CEILING ≈ 135 in score.ts — calibrate with `node tools/calibrate-bands.mjs the and for with national energy` (q ≥ 135 covers ~203 of 48,802 words; document the measured population in the constant's JSDoc); deliberately NOT configurable (08 h2.57). Occurrence-level override: a run member admits regardless of the commonness band, whatever its attestation and whatever lowercase sightings exist — attested → group 1, absent → group 0 — and the override bypasses the conjugation guard (casing evidence outranks morphology, parallel to the properName skip; pin in tests). A member whose q ≥ ceiling is CHAIN-ONLY: never gains admission from casing (run or single), never upserted (store must not see it), but remains in the runs payload so its series bigrams still form and the after-space offer presents its neighbors (typing 'The ' offers 'Fed'). Casing evidence grants candidacy ONLY — ordering unchanged (h2.31). Score battery rides here: run admits 'national'-class at g1, top-band 'The' chain-only (no upsert, bigrams form), guard-bypass pin. Mocking: in-memory dictionary doubles per test/score.test.ts conventions.
4. OUTPUT: occurrence-level admission outcomes + the chain-only member set, consumed by P1.M1.T2.S2 (series bigrams incl. chain-only).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the ceiling constant (population count, calibration command) and the admit() override path in src/core/score.ts. Rides with the work.

subtasks.title: Single mid-sentence capital: relaxed band max(R_eff, 95) + calibrate-bands Cap column update
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: no 95 constant exists anywhere today; rEff (score.ts:188-196) is the existing relaxed-by-length ramp. Memo hazard verified: the SAME raw token at a structural start vs mid-sentence shares ONE memo entry (memo key = token.raw), so a sentenceStart-dependent relaxation CANNOT live in the memo — it must be an occurrence-level override in #replayAdmitMemo (e.g. re-run admit with relaxed opts when the occurrence's casing is 'mid-cap'), keeping #computeAdmitMemo context-free (architecture/01 §5).
2. INPUT: Sighting.casing ('mid-cap' vs 'structural-cap') from P1.M1.T1.S1; the ceiling constant from P1.M1.T3.S1 (chain-only applies to singles too).
3. LOGIC: Implement spec 04 h2.28's casing-evidence paragraphs for singles. A single mid-sentence capital (properName condition — capital NOT at a structural start) admits under the relaxed band max(rEff(len), 95): at group 1 when attested, group 0 when absent. Capitalized candidates at structural starts get NO relaxation (they admit on the merits exactly as their lowercase form). properName drafts keep the conjugation-guard skip (existing behavior, unchanged). Update tools/calibrate-bands.mjs so the Cap column verdicts follow the 95 band + ceiling rules (calibration history in spec 08 stays honest; the tool already prints a Cap: column). Boundary probes ride here: q 94/95/96, structural-start no-relaxation, 'national'-class single admits at g1, top-band single is chain-only. Mocking: score tests with in-memory dict doubles.
4. OUTPUT: occurrence-level relaxed admission for singles; updated calibration tool output (used as evidence in P3.M1.T2.S3 live smoke).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the relaxed-band constant in score.ts + a note in tools/calibrate-bands.mjs that Cap verdicts follow the 95 band/run rules. Rides with the work.

subtasks.title: Pure casing resolver in core + resolver battery
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: no resolver exists; RankedMatch {key, display, description, salience, sessionCount, tier?} (types.ts:165-178) is the object ~20 downstream consumers read (architecture/02 §5). The resolver must live in src/core/ (no pi imports — architecture invariant).
2. INPUT: Candidate tally fields (capCount, lowerCount, capDisplay) from P1.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement spec 04 h2.32 as a pure function resolveCompletionCasing(c: Pick<Candidate, 'key'|'capCount'|'lowerCount'|'capDisplay'>, fragmentFirstLetter: string): string. Fragment begins uppercase → the capitalized form wins; ONLY the first letter is adapted, the rest of the word comes from the winning form's spelling (typed 'Nr' + capDisplay 'NREL' → 'NREL'; + 'National' → 'National'; no capitalized sightings → capitalize the key's first letter; the user's Shift press is never overridden). Fragment lowercase (or zero-fragment) → the form that occurred more often wins (capCount vs lowerCount); ties → lowercase; a word seen only capitalized completes capitalized; words seen only in all caps complete verbatim; paths/technical literals insert verbatim (falls out of the tally rules — pin in tests). Resolver battery rides here: capital-fragment preserve, frequency winner, tie→lower, all-caps verbatim, paths verbatim, zero-fragment listing. Mocking: none — pure function.
4. OUTPUT: the resolver, consumed by P1.M2.T1.S2 (query wiring), P1.M2.T2.S1/S2 (successor labels), P1.M2.T3.S1 (/acwords display).

subtasks.title: Fallback provider: series-first zero-char offers + close-on-space typed arming
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: provider armed branch — successorDisplay at src/pi/provider.ts:436 (store.get(s.next)?.display ?? s.next); zero-char offer arm :462-474 (before === '' || /[ \t]$/ → store.topSuccessors(armed.word), publishChain bare values at prefix ''); fragment arm :501-529 with exact-equal exclusion at :511; close-on-space block starts :528 ('1.8 CLOSE-ON-SPACE'). Typed-word arming does NOT exist today — arming comes only from applyCompletion accepts (architecture/03 §R2).
2. INPUT: Successor.series/nextDisplay + series-aware topSuccessors ordering from P1.M1.T2.S2; resolved display machinery from P1.M2.T1.S2.
3. LOGIC: Implement spec 07 h2.53 on the fallback path. At the armed word-start offer (zero typed chars): successors offered SERIES FIRST (count descending among them), THEN ordinary (count descending) — combined in one published set; series items display and insert their RUN CASING (nextDisplay) at zero typed chars; once the user types, the first-char anchor is case-insensitive as everywhere (matchFragment) and insertion preserves a typed capital first letter (lowercase typing inserts the offer item verbatim). NEW arming transition at the close-on-space site: when a space closes a typed word whose FIRST letter is UPPERCASE and whose lowercase key has series successors (direct topSuccessors consult — series entries included, so chain-only members arm it: typing 'The ' offers 'Fed'), the chain arms; a lowercase typing of the same word must NOT arm (every prose 'the ' would fire). Tab-acceptance arming, the one-shot grant (chain-grant.ts), before_agent_start reset, and the exact-equal exclusion (:511) are UNCHANGED. Chain battery rides here: 'The ' → 'Fed' offer, typed-through disarm, re-arm (test/provider.test.ts + test/chaining-gating.test.ts conventions). Mocking: provider tests with store fixtures + fake current-provider.
4. OUTPUT: series-aware fallback-path behavior; the exact rule set mirrored by P1.M2.T2.S2 on the widget.
